body:
pagerduty-bot: ALERT: high GPU queue depth (pool: inference-eu-west-1) — 95% queue fill, 503 rate of errors > 5m threshold

alia (oncall): seeing it in console too. latency spike -> 95th ~ 2.1s, 99th ~ 6s for text-gen routes. customers hitting 503s. paging eng-runtime.

samir (eng-runtime): on it. any node flaps or driver errors in logs?

alia (oncall): grepping logs now. lots of repeated lines: 
```
[kernel] NVRM: GPU 0: XID 79: GPU has a fault...
containerd: process exited with status 137
```
seems like recurring Xid 79 and OOM kills. autoscaler isn't adding capacity — it's stuck at 40/40 nodes (quota?) and pods are pending because of eviction pressure.

kai (eng-sre): autoscaler logs show `scaleUp` attempts failing: `quotaExceeded` from cloud-provider API. also hitting `PodFitsResources` failures due to GPU driver taints on nodes that restarted.

samir (eng-runtime): Xid 79 typically driver hang/recovery. which driver version?

alia (oncall): nodes show nvidia-driver 525.85.05 on restarted ones; a subset still on 515.x. node restarts correlate with driver restarts — I see kernel messages: `gpu 0000:81:00.0: GPU fault detected: reason 0x2a` repeatedly.

samir (eng-runtime): alright, likely a driver regression + heavy mem footprint causing OOMs under our batching. quick mitigation: reduce max batch size and force fallback to CPU pool for low-priority traffic. can we throttle incoming traffic or set route-based fallback?

alia (oncall): I can flip per-route policy for prod-gen to degrade to smaller model variant and add a 429-based client-side backoff header. deploying a temporary policy now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by alia (oncall) — patching route policy for service/api-gen-prod -> setting model: rdx-compact-v2, max_batch_tokens: 1024, rate_limit: 4000rpm

alia (oncall): done. will monitor. queue depth dropped a bit but still ~70%.

nora (customer-success): flagging top paying customers (acct IDs: C-3489, C-7720) and drafting an incident notice. need ETA for degraded service.

samir (eng-runtime): investigating memory accounting — our allocator shows a hot path holding large KV caches across requests. pushing a hotfix to GC TTL and smaller KV prefetch for live traffic. Will push a runtime config change that reduces per-session KV prefetch from 128 -> 32.

samir (eng-runtime): pushing: `curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/v1/configs/runtime -d '{"kv_prefetch":32}'` (applied to pool inference-eu-west-1).

deploy-bot: runtime config change applied to pool inference-eu-west-1 by samir (eng-runtime)

alia (oncall): autoscaler still reporting `quotaExceeded` on attempted scale. kate from infra mentioned region quota is at limit — infra approval required for emergency quota bump. pinging infra channel.

kai (eng-sre): I can approve emergency scale if infra gives the thumbs up. we also have some nodes flapping because driver update is partially rolled out. we might need to cordon/evict nodes with bad driver and drain them to stable ones.

samir (eng-runtime): workplan: 1) reduce batch & KV prefetch (done), 2) shift lower-tier traffic to CPU fallback, 3) request emergency quota bump (+10 GPUs), 4) identify & isolate nodes with bad driver and roll them back.

alia (oncall): initiating CPU fallback for non-slo routes. routing change queued.

deploy-bot: route change applied — low-priority routes -> cpu-fallback-pool.

alia (oncall): monitoring: low-priority traffic offloaded, queue depth dropped to ~40% over 5m window. error rate for prod-gen dropped from 8% -> 2.5%. good improvement but still seeing Xid churn and two nodes flapping.

kai (eng-sre): infra responded: region GPU quota at 100 total vGPUs, current commit 100. infra ok to approve emergency +8 for 2 hours, need oncall approval for cost.

alia (oncall): approve emergency bump. please execute.

kai (eng-sre): requesting emergency quota bump now. request ID Q-20240301-78.

kate (infra) (via infra channel): granted emergency +8 GPUs to account for 2 hours. confirmed.

kai (eng-sre): autoscaler now can scale. initiating scale-up, but scheduler still delaying because nodes with taints block placement. I'm cordoning two nodes with driver 525.* that are flapping and draining them to let new nodes join.

alia (oncall): commands I'm running: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl cordon gpu-node-23
kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

samir (eng-runtime): we should also mark those nodes with driver-unsafe taint to prevent scheduling until rollback: `kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-17 driver=unsafe:NoSchedule`

alia (oncall): taints applied. pods are rescheduling. new nodes are provisioning.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaled up 6 GPUs in pool inference-eu-west-1 (requested 8). current capacity 46/108 GPUs.

alia (oncall): capacity up, queue depth trending down to 15% in last 3m. Xid errors still present but much less frequent. a couple of containers restarted but downstream error rate stabilized to <1%.

nora (customer-success): drafting update: "We're currently seeing degraded availability for text-generation in EU. We've applied mitigations (fallback, reduced batching, added capacity) — most customers should see improved performance in 10-20m. We're monitoring and will follow up." sending to C-3489 & C-7720 now.

samir (eng-runtime): follow-ups: schedule full rollback of driver 525 to 515 on nodes that flapped, or wait for driver vendor patch? vendor released a patch candidate but not fully validated. I'm leaning rollback -> validate with regression tests.

kai (eng-sre): I recommend rollback on flapped nodes and block driver 525 in the node image until we validate. create a postmortem ticket.

alia (oncall): summarizing for handoff to maria (next oncall):
- Incident: high queue and 503s in inference-eu-west-1 starting 2401234567
- Root cause (probable): driver/runtime instability (Xid 79 / OOM) + autoscaler hit region quota -> prevented immediate scale-up
- Mitigations applied: reduced batch size & KV prefetch, routed lower-priority traffic to CPU fallback, emergency quota bump (+8 GPUs), cordoned/flushed flapping nodes, tainted driver-unsafe nodes, scaled up 6 GPUs, customers notified.
- Current status: degraded -> recovering. queue depth 12%, error rate <1%, Xid events reduced but present.
- Next actions: rollback driver 525 on flapped nodes OR apply vendor patch; full postmortem; long-term: autoscaler should pre-check quota and pre-warm spare capacity for bursty GPU events.

maria (oncall-next): taking handoff. will monitor for 1h and coordinate with samir/kai for driver rollback. thanks alia. :shipit:

alia (oncall): handing off to maria. marking incident as active -> watchlist update.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by maria (oncall-next).

samir (eng-runtime): opened issue #INC-2401: "Xid 79 surge + autoscale quota block -> recovery & driver rollback plan" with proposed timeline and regression tests. tagging eng-runtime, eng-sre, infra.

nora (customer-success): I'll send a 1h follow-up to customers with current status and next ETA for full remediation.

maria (oncall-next): quick note: if Xid flares again, we'll enable circuit-breaker on the highest-throughput route to limit burst concurrency to 4 concurrent requests per key.

alia (oncall): copy. I'll keep a short post-incident log in ops-runbook with commands used.

samir (eng-runtime): thanks all. monitoring dashboard shows sustained improvement. will keep runbook steps and logs attached to #INC-2401.

(End of thread)
